symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: The index of an axis of the array, from 1 to d.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

symbols.name: axis position count
symbols.meaning: The number of positions along axis i.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

symbols.name: index tuple
symbols.meaning: The tuple of coordinates (j_1,...,j_d) of an entry of the array.
symbols.quote: An entry of the array $u$ has an index tuple $j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$ with $0\le j_i<q_i$.

symbols.name: output index tuple
symbols.meaning: An output index tuple shaped like j.
symbols.quote:
With $k$ an output index tuple shaped like $j$,
$$(F_{\boldsymbol q}u)_k=\frac1{\prod_i q_i}\sum_j u_j\,e^{-2\pi i\sum_i j_ik_i/q_i}.$$

symbols.name: axis operator
symbols.meaning: An operator on sequences of length q_i, applied to every line along axis i.
symbols.quote: For operators $G_i$ on sequences of length $q_i$, the tensor product $\bigotimes_i G_i$ applies each $G_i$ to every line along axis $i$.

symbols.name: time-bound slack
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant with 0<delta<1/8 that sets the slack in the exponent 3/2+delta of p in the time bound.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

symbols.name: resampling parameter
symbols.meaning: An integer resampling parameter with 2<=alpha<sqrt p.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

symbols.meaning: The tuple of source axis lengths (s_1,...,s_d).
symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.name: padded lengths
symbols.meaning: The tuple of padded power-of-two axis lengths (t_1,...,t_d).
symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.meaning: The total exponent 2d alpha^2 of the power of two multiplying the tensored identity.
symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the source index permutations P_{s_i}; here not the scalar ring.

symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the index permutations P_{t_i}.
symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional input maps A_i.
symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

symbols.name: source axis permutation
symbols.meaning: The index permutation of source axis i.
symbols.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

symbols.name: padded axis permutation
symbols.meaning: The index permutation of padded axis i.
symbols.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

symbols.name: axis input map
symbols.meaning: The linear input map of axis i.
symbols.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

symbols.name: axis output map
symbols.meaning: The linear output map of axis i.
symbols.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

symbols.name: axis transform
symbols.meaning: The one-dimensional normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q_i.
symbols.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

symbols.name: multidimensional transform
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the axis transforms F_{q_i}.
symbols.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

symbols.name: axis operator X
symbols.meaning: An operator on axis i.
symbols.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

symbols.name: axis operator Y
symbols.meaning: An operator on axis i.
symbols.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

relations.predicate: is the tensor product of one-dimensional
relations.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.
Each line transform is computed by the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) in $O(t_i\log t_i)$ operations.
